summary: Filed from a live report: an agent instance from npm run app:isolated hit Generation failed / port 48188 in use, while the port was held by the users OWN engine (PID 10372, child of server fork 8040). Root is that /comfy/start and /comfy/status both read activeComfyProcess, which answers did I spawn it rather than is an engine up.
todo -> doing. Created directly in doing: the root was traced and the fix scoped before the card was cut, and the user has already made the product call that 48188 is shared across app instances.

doing -> done (complete). /comfy/start now ATTACHES to an engine it did not spawn and /comfy/status probes the shared port before reporting the engine down. Proven live with the users app on :3000 and its engine on 48188 (PID 10372): a second instance from npm run app:isolated got status running:true ready:true and start HTTP 200 Already running, where it previously got the 409 dialog, and the owner engine was still LISTENING afterwards. Stop safety proven by reading stopComfyUI - its whole body is behind the null check, no kill-by-port - rather than firing a kill at a live engine. comfy-port-lockstep asserted the OLD contract and failed correctly; rewritten to the new one keeping the probe-before-spawn invariant, which matters MORE now since falling through to spawn on an occupied port leaves a dead engine. 7/7 green, eslint clean. Known gap logged not hidden: a non-owner restart cannot actually restart, so it warns.
Archived out of board.columns.done to .agents/mpi-kanban/tasks/_archived/MPI-484/ (workspace preserved intact). mpi-archive run 2026-08-21.
